title: Nosebleed treatment
what: The doctor finds where the blood is coming from and stops it. Sometimes the vessel is sealed with cautery, or the nose is packed.
why: When a nosebleed will not stop on its own or keeps coming back.
duration: usually 15 to 30 minutes; if the nose is packed, the packing usually comes out after 1 to 2 days
tell_doctor: Blood thinners. Do not stop them on your own

prepare.title: Right now
prepare.text: Sit up and lean your head forward, not back. Pinch the soft part of your nose firmly for 10 to 15 minutes.

prepare.title: What not to do
prepare.text: Do not tilt your head back or swallow the blood.

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: If you take blood thinners, tell your doctor. Do not stop them on your own.

steps: The doctor clears clots from your nose
The lining is numbed with a spray or cotton pads
It is sealed with cautery, or the nose is packed
Sometimes your blood pressure is checked
You are told what to do at home
feel: Packing makes it hard to breathe through your nose and makes your eyes water
after: Do not blow or pick your nose for a few days
No heavy lifting or hot drinks in the first days
If your nose is packed, it will be removed at the clinic
Keep the air moist at home
red_flags: Bleeding will not stop after 20 minutes, or is heavy: call emergency services
A nosebleed after a head injury: call emergency services

faq.q: Why not tilt my head back?
faq.a: Blood runs into your throat, you swallow it, and you may vomit.

faq.q: Why do I get nosebleeds often?
faq.a: Often from dry air and fragile vessels. Your doctor will find the cause.

reminders.text: Nosebleed appointment in an hour. Bring your medicine list.
